neighbours.label: locative preposition (on, in, upon) saying where something is built or erected
fire: The settlers built cabins on the riverbank.
The company erected warehouses on reclaimed land.
Monks built a monastery in the mountains.
The emperor ordered a palace built on the hill.
Farmers constructed terraces on the steep slopes.
The town built a new school in the old quarter.
A lighthouse was built upon the rocks.
Engineers are building a dam in the gorge.
quiet: The settlers depended on the riverbank.
The company spent heavily on reclaimed land.
The emperor ordered a palace built by slaves.
The town built a new school for the children.
A lighthouse was painted with stripes.
Engineers are building a dam for the city.

notes: Probes: built + on/in/upon fires, and on/in after other verbs is quiet. 'built by' and 'built with' are quiet, so the pole marks the site slot rather than the verb.
